<action type="say">
Here’s a concrete plan for your workshop.

1) Date, time, and weather/back‑up
- Primary date: Sunday, December 14, morning (for example 10:00 am–12:00 pm).
- Forecast for Dec 14 in Madison (from the tool): about 27°F, cloudy, low chance of precip, light wind. Cold but workable with warm clothing and hot drinks.
- Simple go/no‑go rule you can share:
  - Run as scheduled unless:
    - Temperature or windchill is below 10°F, or
    - There’s steady rain, sleet, or heavy snow during the workshop time.
- Backup “weather date”: pick the following weekend morning (e.g., Sat Dec 20 or Sun Dec 21, same time).
  - Advertise as: “Sat Dec 14, 10am–12pm (backup weather date: Sun Dec 21, 10am–12pm).”
  - Decide by 5pm the day before if you’re moving to the backup, and say exactly where you’ll post updates.

2) 2‑hour sample agenda (10:00–12:00, outdoor, no power, limited seating)

- 10:00–10:10 (10 min) – Welcome & warm‑up
  - Quick welcome, your role, goals for the session.
  - Ask “What brought you here?” – 1–2 quick responses.
  - Hand out a 1‑page “What goes in our compost” sheet.

- 10:10–10:30 (20 min) – Composting basics (standing near bins)
  - Essentials: greens vs browns, air, moisture, time.
  - Very concrete for your site:
    - What food scraps are allowed.
    - What yard waste is welcome.
    - What is never allowed (plastic, compostable cups, meat/dairy, etc.).
  - Show a simple diagram of your bin system if you can print one.

- 10:30–11:10 (40 min) – Demo & hands‑on at the bins
  - Walk through existing bins: show active, resting, and finished (if you have those stages).
  - Live demo:
    - Add a small bucket of “good” scraps.
    - Cover with browns.
    - Turn/aerate a section with a fork.
    - Check moisture and smell (“forest, not garbage”).
  - Rotate 3–5 volunteers at a time to:
    - Add a small amount of material correctly.
    - Try turning/aerating.
  - While people are rotating, take questions informally.

- 11:10–11:30 (20 min) – How to use THESE bins correctly
  - “User journey”:
    - Where to come in,
    - Which bin to use,
    - Where to find browns,
    - What to do if bins are full.
  - Point to clear signs you’ll install on the bins and nearby.
  - Explain who maintains the system and what help is useful (regular turning, bringing browns, reporting problems).

- 11:30–11:50 (20 min) – Q&A and troubleshooting
  - Invite questions about:
    - Common confusions (compostable packaging, coffee filters, citrus, weeds, diseased plants).
    - Home vs shared composting.
  - Share 2–3 common mistakes you already see at the garden and how to fix them.

- 11:50–12:00 (10 min) – Wrap‑up & next steps
  - Re‑cap the 3–5 key rules for using the garden bins.
  - Invite sign‑ups:
    - Email list / text group / volunteer list for compost work days.
  - Remind people where to find the rules (signs, website, bulletin board).

3) Materials & logistics checklist (no power, limited seating)

- Teaching/communication
  - 1‑page handout: “How to use the [Garden Name] compost bins”
    - YES list (with icons/pictures if possible).
    - NO list.
    - Simple diagram of bin layout.
  - Laminated signs/posters:
    - At drop‑off point: “Add food scraps here” with simple YES/NO icons.
    - Above browns: “Always cover food scraps with browns.”
    - On or near bins: “Garden Compost Rules” with your top 5 rules.
  - Clipboards + pens for:
    - Sign‑in sheet (name, email).
    - Volunteer interest.

- Physical setup
  - A few folding chairs for those who need to sit, plus 1–2 tables if available.
  - Entrance sign: “COMPOST WORKSHOP →”.
  - Warmth/comfort:
    - Thermoses with hot tea/coffee/cider.
    - Optional: hand warmers, extra gloves.
    - Encourage people in your outreach to “dress warmly for standing outside.”

- Tools & demo materials
  - Pitchfork(s), shovel(s), compost aerator if you have it.
  - 1 bucket of clean, “good” food scraps.
  - 1–2 buckets of browns (leaves, straw, shredded paper).
  - Work gloves in multiple sizes.
  - Rake and extra bucket for tidying if anything spills.

- Admin & weather plan
  - Written weather policy + backup date in your notes and on your flyer/social posts.
  - Plan for how you’ll notify people (email list, social media, garden bulletin board).

4) Sample outreach text (adapt as needed)

Title:  
“Community Garden Composting Workshop – Learn to Use Our Bins”

Body:  
“Join us for a free, hands-on composting workshop at the [Garden Name] in Madison!

Date: Saturday, December 14, 10:00 am–12:00 pm  
Location: [Garden Name & address]  
Who: Garden members and general public, ages [X+].  

We’ll cover composting basics and show you exactly how to use our garden’s compost bins so we get more good compost and less contamination. Expect a short talk, live demos at the bins, and plenty of time for questions.

Dress warmly—we’ll be outside the whole time. We’ll provide hot drinks.

Weather plan: We’ll go ahead unless it’s dangerously cold or there’s heavy rain/snow. If we need to postpone, we’ll move to our backup date of [Backup Date] and post updates at [where you’ll post, e.g., Facebook page, website, garden bulletin board].

Space is limited to 25 people. Please RSVP at [email or sign-up link].”

What would you like to refine next:  
- the exact YES/NO list and bin signage,  
- the 1‑page handout, or  
- a short script/notes for your 20‑minute “composting basics” talk?</action>
